placement.position_note: Interpretive placement on a GENERATED lot, not a recovered parcel. The lot geometry is the K7 plat module's — this project has never read Thompson's numbering off a sheet, and the side lot lines and the alley are conjectural even where the block face is not. The building stands 1.6 m back from its street edge, which is a typology for the period and not a measurement of this lot. persons.name: Fred'k. Curtenius
persons.note: PROJECTED RESIDENT. Documented in Chicago post-office evidence but not independently corroborated strongly enough for attested circa-1835 residence. KNOWN ONLY FROM THE POST OFFICE, IN ONE RETURN. The papers print 'Curtenius, Fred'k.' in a single return of letters uncalled-for at the Chicago post office — the Democrat of 1 July 1835, column 4 — dated 1835-07-01. Nothing else in the corpus names this person: no trade, no street, no household, no arrival, so every other claim here is written unattested in its own block. WHAT THAT IS WORTH: a correspondent believed a person of this name reachable at Chicago on that date, and nothing further — not that they lived here, kept a trade here, or were here on 1 July 1835. It is the weakest evidence this project accepts for a resident, and a source placing them elsewhere retires the record. THE ARGUMENT EVERY RECORD OF THIS KIND SHARES is written once instead of once per file: the ruling of 2026-08-30 and what it cost the town (docs/LIBERTIES.md L214), the refusals and the transcription standard behind the reading (tools/mint_letter_list_residents.py). No figure is drawn (L1).

residents.research_note: MINTED FROM THE LETTER LISTS (T-0378, T-0379). THE HOUSEHOLD IS A CONTAINER, NOT AN ARGUMENT: every other record here argues for a household, and this one argues for a PERSON. `data/residents/` cannot carry a person outside a household, so one was written around them and told to claim nothing — one member, no dwelling, no division, no trade, no family, no arrival beyond the paper's bound. tools/mint_letter_list_residents.py derives the set and prints every refusal, `--gate` proves no record here gained a roof, a trade or a second member, and docs/LIBERTIES.md L214 carries the change of scale.

persons.name: Ke Way Quam
persons.note: CARDED FROM THE BORDERLINE ROSTER'S R6 (T-1376, stage `underdocumented`). Enrolled at Chicago in 1832 in the company the Black Hawk War roll heads INDIAN, with no 1835 corroboration and no card. The licence is R3's — the same roll, the same year, the same page — and the twenty men of Kercheval's company the town already carries were re-admitted under it. The roll prints him as `KE WAY QUAM`, company `INDIAN`, enrolled at `CHICAGO`. The research READ this name and WITHHELD it, and that refusal is not overturned: this record is a reconstruction of what the town looks like if the name is admitted at the limit of its own evidence, and it says so on its face. The reading, the source and the refusal stand at `civic:data/research/civic/records/blackhawk_war_1832_chicago.json#records/blackhawk_1832_043#0` in data/reconstruction/1835_borderline_roster.json. REVIEW REQUIRED: this card is a record of a Native person at Chicago in the three years of the removal, and AGENTS.md's standing constraint holds it for review by Native scholars or community organisations before any scene carrying it may be marked released. Enrolled at Chicago in 1832 in the company the Black Hawk War roll heads INDIAN, with no 1835 corroboration and no card. The licence is R3's — the same roll, the same year, the same page — and the twenty men of Kercheval's company the town already carries were re-admitted under it. The roll prints him as `PAY CO JE BAI`, company `INDIAN`, enrolled at `CHICAGO`. The research READ this name and WITHHELD it, and that refusal is not overturned: this record is a reconstruction of what the town looks like if the name is admitted at the limit of its own evidence, and it says so on its face. The reading, the source and the refusal stand at `civic:data/research/civic/records/blackhawk_war_1832_chicago.json#records/blackhawk_1832_086#0` in data/reconstruction/1835_borderline_roster.json. REVIEW REQUIRED: this card is a record of a Native person at Chicago in the three years of the removal, and AGENTS.md's standing constraint holds it for review by Native scholars or community organisations before any scene carrying it may be marked released. No figure is drawn (L1).

residents.research_note: WRITTEN BY tools/reconstruct_underdocumented.py (T-1376), the `native_and_metis` half of the `underdocumented` stage of the 1835 resident reconstruction programme, under the owner's ruling of 2026-09-17 recorded in AGENTS.md. This file is NOT research and is not a mint output: data/residents/households/ is re-derived by the mint writers and data/residents/index.json is derived from that directory, so a card written here lives beside the re-admissions and is overlaid onto the scene by tools/compile_scene.py. REVIEW REQUIRED AND TOUCHES REMOVAL, both true, for the subject this record is about: a Native man at Chicago in 1832, three years before the removal of the Potawatomi from this place, inside the project's first target year. The review AGENTS.md commits to has not been held; until it is, no scene carrying this card may be marked released. docs/RESEARCH/native_and_metis_1835.md lists every source read and what is still owed. docs/LIBERTIES.md carries the invention.

what_it_supplies: A 665-roof production target with independently reconcilable group, district, level, and construction totals.
Thirty-five architectural family definitions with dimensional and massing bands.
District character, spacing, variation, finish, and chronology constraints for a July 1835 reconstruction.
A required distinction between named documentary landmarks and anonymous inferred infill.
what_it_does_not_supply: A surviving July 1835 building census or parcel-by-parcel roof register.
Exact locations, dimensions, appearance, occupants, or construction dates for anonymous roofs.
Authority to replace stronger building-specific evidence already represented in the dataset.

research_note: RECONSTRUCTED / GENERATED, NOT AN ATTESTED NAMED BUILDING. The block, its scheduled roof count and its family mix follow the 665-roof programme; exact presence, lot, position, footprint, finish and instance-level form are interpretive. The H3 boarding house resolves through the frame_tavern archetype, the crosswalk's placeholder for it; the canonical boarding_house_frame generator is not implemented. The tavern's own cues are not raised on it: no gallery, no frontispiece, no sign, and a kitchen door rather than a carriage door in the rear service wing.

fabric_basis.words: whitewashed clapboard on a balloon frame under a new roof — a boarding house, new-built (rule F-B: a boarding-house or tavern keeper's by its type)

sizes.upper_windows: ceil(30 crowded beds / 3 to a chamber) = 10, held to the crosswalk's 6-10 = 10, then to the 8 sashes a front of 9.96 m carries at 1.15 m a bay: 8 across the upper storey of the front and of the rear
sizes.stovepipes: ceil(13 ordinary beds / 3 to a stove) = 5, held to 2-6: 5
sizes.chimneys: not sized by the beds: the two brick stacks are the family's kitchen and common-room hearths, and the stoves the beds add go out through the roof as stovepipes

lodging.note: The town model puts a boarding house at 9 people on an ordinary night and 21 when full, from the 1840 household tail (p90 and p99 of 964 Chicago households). This building takes the share of its class's total that its 289 m² of enclosed floor (145 m² × 2 storeys) is of the class's floor area.
lodging.replaceable_by: Any source that states this house's rooms, beds or lodgers on a dated day: an advertisement counting its rooms, a traveller's account of how many it slept, a licence return. A stated capacity retires the apportioned one outright.
